# Foreword {.unnumbered}

Magnetic linear and angular position measurement systems have become indispensable in modern automation, drive, and automotive technology. Their core component—the magnetic measurement scale—is, however, developed, manufactured, magnetized, and tested by very different stakeholders across the entire value chain. It is precisely at these interfaces that the lack of a common and unambiguous language repeatedly becomes apparent.

DIN SPEC 91411 [@DIN91411] represented an important first step toward addressing this issue. Practical work with this specification over the past years has clearly confirmed the value of a uniform description, while at the same time showing that several key terms were understood and interpreted differently in everyday use. This experience gave rise to the desire to sharpen existing definitions, close gaps, and consistently derive the representation rules from physical principles.

The present guideline is the result of this further development. It was prepared by a consortium of member companies and institutes of INNOMAG e. V., bringing manufacturers, users, and research institutions together. In this composition, the document reflects the collective practical experience of the professional community and pursues a clear objective: to establish a common and generally understandable terminology for magnetic measurement scales that avoids misunderstandings and facilitates technical exchange across company and national boundaries.

Special thanks are due to Dr. Michael Ortner of Silicon Austria Labs, who made a major contribution to the preparation of this guideline. We also thank all contributing authors as well as the participating companies and institutes, without whose commitment this document would not have been possible.

We wish all readers an informative and stimulating read and hope that this guideline will find as broad a practical application as its predecessor.

# Abbreviations and Symbols {.unnumbered}

## List of Abbreviations {.unlisted}

| Abbreviation | Meaning |
|---|---|
| CS | coordinate system |
| IP | in-plane |
| OOP | out-of-plane |

## List of Symbols for Fundamental Quantities {.unlisted}

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $\vec{B}$ | magnetic flux density, B-field | T |
| $\vec{H}$ | magnetic field strength, H-field | A/m |
| $\vec{M}$ | magnetization | A/m |
| $\vec{J}$ | magnetic polarization | T |
| $\mu_0$ | vacuum permeability | T m/A |
| $p$ | coordinate in longitudinal direction | m or ° |
| $o$ | coordinate in transverse direction | m |
| $n$ | coordinate in normal direction; measurement height where applicable | m |
| $o$ | origin of a coordinate system | – |
| $\vec{e}_p$ | unit vector in $p$-direction | – |
| $\vec{e}_o$ | unit vector in $o$-direction | – |
| $\vec{e}_n$ | unit vector in $n$-direction | – |
| $\vec{r}$ | position vector | m |
